titulo: Module 01 — Quiz: the exam, the Messages API, and the request surface

questoes.pergunta: How many scenarios appear in a single sitting of the CCAR-F exam?
opcoes: All 6 scenarios in the bank, always
4 scenarios randomly drawn from a bank of 6
2 fixed scenarios and 2 randomly drawn ones
One scenario per exam domain, i.e., 5 scenarios in total
questoes.explicacao: The exam randomly draws 4 of the 6 scenarios in the bank, and the questions hang off them.
feedbacks: Incorrect: there are 6 in the bank, but only 4 make it into each sitting.
Correct: 4 of 6, randomly drawn.
Incorrect: there are no fixed scenarios; all of them come from the random draw.
Incorrect: scenarios don't map 1:1 to domains; a single scenario mixes several domains.

questoes.pergunta: Which domain carries the HIGHEST weight on the exam?
opcoes: D4 — Prompt engineering & structured output
D3 — Claude Code configuration & workflows
D2 — Tool design & MCP integration
D1 — Agentic architecture & orchestration
questoes.explicacao: D1 weighs 27%; D3 and D4 weigh 20% each, D2 18%, and D5 15%.
feedbacks: Incorrect: D4 weighs 20%.
Incorrect: D3 weighs 20%.
Incorrect: D2 weighs 18%.
Correct: D1 = 27%, more than a quarter of the exam.

questoes.pergunta: You have 3 minutes left and 4 unanswered questions. What is the best course of action?
opcoes: Mark an option on all of them, since there is no penalty for guessing
Leave the ones you don't know blank, so you don't lose points
Answer only the single-answer ones and leave the 'Choose TWO' ones blank
Review the ones already answered instead of answering the new ones
questoes.explicacao: With no penalty for guessing, a blank answer is a guaranteed lost point; guessing can only help.
feedbacks: Correct: no penalty, so always mark an answer.
Incorrect: there is no deduction for wrong answers; a blank is worth zero either way.
Incorrect: even on multiple-response questions, guessing has a chance of being right; a blank has none.
Incorrect: reviewing doesn't make up for leaving questions unanswered.

questoes.pergunta: One option proposes enforcing the US$500 refund limit solely through an emphatic instruction in the system prompt. Which exam principle does it violate?
opcoes: Measure before changing anything
Use few-shot examples for edge cases
A critical (financial) rule belongs in deterministic code, not in the prompt
Always prefer the most capable model
questoes.explicacao: A prompt is probabilistic, with a nonzero failure rate. A financial limit requires deterministic enforcement (hook/validation).
feedbacks: Incorrect: measuring matters, but the problem here is where the rule is enforced.
Incorrect: few-shot is still prompting; it provides no guarantee.
Correct: financial consequence → hook or validation in code.
Incorrect: no model turns a prompt into a guarantee.

questoes.pergunta: Which of these is the CORRECT way for the loop to decide whether the agent has finished?
opcoes: Look for the word 'FINAL' in the response text
Check the response's stop_reason
Stop when the response has no text block
Stop after 10 iterations
questoes.explicacao: stop_reason is the loop's control signal: tool_use continues, end_turn ends.
feedbacks: Incorrect: anti-pattern #1, parsing natural language to decide when it's done.
Correct: stop_reason decides.
Incorrect: the presence or absence of text doesn't indicate completion; text and tool_use can coexist.
Incorrect: anti-pattern #2, an arbitrary limit as the primary mechanism (it only serves as a backstop).

questoes.pergunta: The model's response contains a text block ('Let me check the order') and a tool_use block. What does this mean?
opcoes: It hasn't finished yet: execute the tool and return the result
The model has finished; the tool_use is merely informational
The response is malformed and should be discarded
You must choose between displaying the text or executing the tool
questoes.explicacao: content can mix text and tool_use. With stop_reason tool_use, execute the tool and continue the loop.
feedbacks: Correct: having text doesn't mean it has finished.
Incorrect: tool_use is a request for execution, not a comment.
Incorrect: mixing blocks is normal and valid.
Incorrect: there's no choice to make; the text is a preamble and the tool needs to run.

questoes.pergunta: The model requested 3 tools in the same response and one of them failed. How should you return the results?
opcoes: Three separate user messages, one per tool_result
Only the two successful results, omitting the one that failed
One user message with the first result, then send the rest later
One user message with all three tool_result blocks (the failure with is_error: true)
questoes.explicacao: All tool_result blocks go in a single user message, each with its tool_use_id; the failure gets is_error: true so the model can reason about recovery.
feedbacks: Incorrect: spreading results across several messages breaks the protocol and discourages parallel calls.
Incorrect: omitting the failure is error suppression (anti-pattern #7) and leaves a tool_use without a result.
Incorrect: all pending results must go together.
Correct: one message, three results, failure flagged.

questoes.pergunta: What links a tool_result to the tool request that originated it?
opcoes: The tool name
The order of the blocks in the message
A tool_use_id equal to the id of the tool_use block
The message's index in the history
questoes.explicacao: Each tool_result references the exact id of the corresponding tool_use in tool_use_id.
feedbacks: Incorrect: the same tool can be called several times; the name doesn't identify the call.
Incorrect: the link is by id, not by position.
Correct: the exact tool_use_id.
Incorrect: the message index isn't used for this.

questoes.pergunta: An extraction has started returning JSON that is cut off at the end on long documents. Which stop_reason do you expect to see?
opcoes: max_tokens
stop_sequence
refusal
pause_turn
questoes.explicacao: Output truncated at the output ceiling yields stop_reason max_tokens; raise the limit or continue.
feedbacks: Correct: it hit the output ceiling.
Incorrect: stop_sequence indicates the model hit a configured stop sequence, not truncation.
Incorrect: refusal is a safety refusal.
Incorrect: pause_turn belongs to the server-side tool loop.

questoes.pergunta: Why can a model refusal go unnoticed in code that only checks the HTTP status?
opcoes: Because the refusal comes with HTTP 500
Because the refusal arrives with HTTP 200 and stop_reason refusal
Because the refusal only shows up in the server logs
Because the refusal comes as a timeout exception
questoes.explicacao: From an HTTP standpoint, a refusal is a successful response; the signal is in stop_reason: refusal.
feedbacks: Incorrect: it's not a server error.
Correct: HTTP 200 + stop_reason refusal.
Incorrect: it comes in the response itself.
Incorrect: it's not a timeout.

questoes.pergunta: Which statement about the Tool Runner is correct?
opcoes: It is the same product as the Claude Agent SDK
It hosts the loop and a per-session sandbox on Anthropic's infrastructure, with versioned configs
It ships with built-in tools such as Read, Edit, and Bash
A helper in the API SDK that runs the loop over your tools, on your infrastructure
questoes.explicacao: The Tool Runner automates request → execute → repeat for your own tools only. Built-in tools belong to the Agent SDK; hosting belongs to Managed Agents.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Tool Runner ≠ Agent SDK (a classic trap).
Incorrect: that describes Managed Agents.
Incorrect: built-in tools come with the Agent SDK.
Correct: just the loop, just your tools, on your infrastructure.

questoes.pergunta: On recent models, how do you ask the model to decide on its own how much to think?
opcoes: thinking: {type: enabled, budget_tokens: 8000}
temperature: 0
thinking: {type: adaptive}
An assistant prefill starting with '<thinking>'
questoes.explicacao: Adaptive thinking replaces budget_tokens; on newer models, budget_tokens returns a 400.
feedbacks: Incorrect: budget_tokens is the old format and returns a 400 on newer models.
Incorrect: temperature doesn't control reasoning and is rejected on newer models.
Correct: adaptive.
Incorrect: prefill returns a 400 on newer models.

questoes.pergunta: Where does the effort parameter go in the request?
opcoes: At the top level of the request, alongside model
Inside output_config
Inside the thinking block
In the system prompt, as text
feedbacks: Incorrect: it's not a top-level parameter.
Correct: output_config.effort.
Incorrect: thinking only sets the mode (adaptive).
Incorrect: effort is an API parameter, not a text instruction.

questoes.pergunta: A team is about to migrate to a newer model. Which step does the exam expect?
opcoes: Swap the model ID directly in production and monitor the rate of 400 errors over the first few hours
Copy the same parameters, since the API is the same
Increase max_tokens to compensate for the changes
Test the request shape on the new model and recalibrate effort
questoes.explicacao: Accepted parameters change from model to model (budget_tokens, sampling, prefill, and forced tool_choice can return a 400); test and recalibrate beforehand.
feedbacks: Incorrect: discovering 400s in production is exactly what you want to avoid.
Incorrect: the endpoint is the same, but the accepted surface changes per model.
Incorrect: it doesn't address the problem of rejected parameters.
Correct: test the request shape and recalibrate.

questoes.pergunta: A developer wants to guarantee consistent JSON on a newer model. Which TWO approaches are valid? (Choose TWO.)
opcoes: An assistant prefill starting with '{'
temperature: 0 and top_p: 0.1
Structured outputs via output_config.format with a JSON schema
Increase budget_tokens so the model thinks more about the format
A clear format instruction in the system prompt
questoes.explicacao: Prefill, sampling, and budget_tokens are rejected on newer models. Structured outputs provide a schema guarantee; an instruction in the system prompt is the textual substitute.
feedbacks: Incorrect: prefill returns a 400 on newer models.
Incorrect: sampling parameters are rejected on newer models and don't guarantee format.
Correct: structural guarantee.
Incorrect: budget_tokens returns a 400 on newer models and doesn't guarantee format.
Correct: the recommended substitute for prefill when structured outputs aren't used.
